The outlined treatment plan for acute bacterial sinusitis is appropriate and aligns with current clinical guidelines. Amoxicillin-clavulanate is considered a first-line antibiotic therapy for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis, particularly in cases where risk factors for resistance are present or when initial monotherapy with amoxicillin is deemed insufficient. The addition of nasal saline irrigation helps to clear mucus and reduce inflammation, while oral decongestants provide symptomatic relief. The instruction to return for evaluation if symptoms persist beyond seven days or worsen is a standard safety measure to ensure the infection is resolving and to prevent complications.
